{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement

**To:** Deal team (Sparkling)  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Garman software licence and maintenance agreement  
**Status:** 19 rules assessed — 8 deviations, 8 compliant, 3 missing clauses

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial posture is better than expected in several respects: there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment, liquidated-damages or audit obligation on us anywhere in the document, and our termination-for-convenience right (90 days' notice, no exit fee) sits at the fallback with no reciprocal convenience right for Garman.

The concerns are concentrated in four areas. First, and most seriously, Section 15 carries no aggregate liability cap at all despite its heading, leaving direct-damages exposure unlimited on both sides and with no gross negligence or wilful misconduct exclusions. Second, the assignment regime is closed: Section 20(d) requires consent for any assignment with no M&A carve-out or reasonableness standard, and Section 3(c) bars Sparkling from assigning at all — a position that approaches walk-away. Third, our licence and IP position is thin: Garman owns all IP including the Improvements and Schedule "D" Modifications we pay for, while our licence is non-exclusive, non-transferable, location-limited and contingent on continued fee payment. Fourth, three clauses the playbook expects are simply absent — a renewal mechanic for the maintenance term, post-termination transition assistance and data return, and any vendor insurance covenant.

We have also redlined governing law (Nova Scotia, the vendor's home jurisdiction, is outside the accepted list), the Section 19 no-hire (which bars hiring *any* employee of the other party for the term plus one year), the Section 13 indemnity (no duty to defend, no refund where the procure/modify/replace remedies fail), and the Section 12 warranty (no services warranty, no warranty remedy after acceptance).

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability |
| 2 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(d); § 3(c)) |
| 3 | High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity |
| 4 | High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at fallback) | § 17 Term and Termination |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees |
| 12 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 12 Specifications and Warranty |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Missing | § 10 Maintenance and Support |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Page 10 (§ 20) |

### Deviation detail and our proposals

**LOL-CAP (critical) — § 15.** No "exceed" or "aggregate liability" language exists anywhere, so direct-damages exposure is unlimited. The mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the carve-outs for Section 13 (IP indemnity) and Section 14 (confidentiality) already satisfy the fallback carve-outs, but the absence of any cap and of gross negligence / wilful misconduct exclusions fails the fallback on material terms. *Proposal:* add a mutual 12-month fees cap inside Section 15 (so the existing exclusions continue to apply) and carve out gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

**ASSIGN (high) — § 20(d) and § 3(c).** Section 20(d) requires the other party's consent for any assignment, with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard; Section 3(c) separately prohibits Sparkling from assigning at all absent Garman's written authorisation. That fails the fallback and, as to § 3(c), approaches walk-away. There is no change-of-control clause, so Garman has no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right. *Proposal:* mutual successor assignment on written notice, other assignments subject to consent not unreasonably withheld; delete the conflicting assignment words from § 3(c).

**INDEMN (high) — § 13.** Section 13 itself is only an ownership statement; the operative indemnity in the following paragraph is limited to Losses from breach of Garman's title/quiet-enjoyment warranty, with procure/replace/modify remedies and a ten-day notice condition. It is uncapped (§ 15 disapplies the limit to § 13), which is better than the fallback 3x super-cap, and has no customer-modification/combination exclusions. It nonetheless fails the fallback because there is no refund where the procure/modify/replace remedies are unavailable, and it lacks any duty to defend, affiliate coverage, or indemnity for breach of law, Garman-caused unauthorised access to our data, or Garman's gross negligence/wilful misconduct. *Proposal:* add a Garman defence-and-indemnity paragraph with claim procedure, targeting the preferred position rather than importing the fallback super-cap (which would weaken our current uncapped position), and confirm that any Sparkling indemnity stays limited to our content and our breach of law.

**IP (high) — § 2, § 13, § 17(a), § 4(b).** Garman owns all IP in the Work, including Improvements and the Schedule "D" Modifications we pay for, while our licence is capped to Authorized Locations, expressly non-sublicensable and lasts only while fees are paid and the Agreement is not terminated. Nothing limits Garman's use of our converted data. *Proposal (fallback):* preserve Garman's ownership; add perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide and royalty-free modifiers plus rights to use, modify and sublicense; carve the § 2 licence out of the § 17(a) termination mechanic; delete only the conflicting sublicence bar; extend the grant to Improvements and Modifications; limit Garman's use of our data to providing the services. *(Note: this finding required repair during verification and should be re-read against the final redline.)*

**LICENSE (high) — § 2, § 3(c).** The grant already covers our affiliated companies at Authorized Locations with no notice condition, and is not revocable at Garman's discretion. But it is expressly "non-transferable" and § 3(c) bars transfer without consent, so the fallback M&A-transferability element fails. *Proposal:* make the licence transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition, with a matching carve-out in § 3(c).

**GOVLAW (medium) — § 20(h).** Nova Scotia law and non-exclusive Nova Scotia jurisdiction — the vendor's home forum, outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales). No arbitration clause exists. *Proposal:* New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County.

**NOSOLICIT (medium) — § 19.** This is a no-hire, not a non-solicit: it bars each party and its affiliates from hiring any employee of the other for the term plus one year, with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs. A no-hire covering all personnel is walk-away territory notwithstanding mutuality. *Proposal (fallback):* mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services for 12 months after involvement ends, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and express confirmation that hiring is not prohibited.

**WARRANTY (medium) — § 12.** The one-year (and continuing) Specifications conformance warranty satisfies the fallback software element, but nothing warrants Maintenance Services quality and § 12 provides no remedy — repair sits only in § 10(c), and the only refund is the acceptance-period rejection right in §§ 7–8, which expires on acceptance. There is no general disclaimer that would swallow an added warranty. *Proposal:* add a 30-day Maintenance Services warranty and a repair/replace/refund remedy.

**RENEWAL (medium) — missing.** The only renewal language is the description of the maintenance term as a "renewable one-year term"; nothing states how it renews, gives us a non-renewal window, or caps renewal fee increases. *Proposal:* automatic 12-month renewals, 30-day Sparkling opt-out, 60-day Garman reminder, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

**TRANSITION (medium) — missing.** Section 17 covers only our return of Garman's materials; neither § 17, § 18 (survival), § 16 (escrow) nor § 14 requires Garman to provide exit assistance or to return or delete our data. *Proposal:* six months' assistance at then-current rates, data return in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion after return.

**INSURANCE (low, but see walk-away below) — missing.** No insurance clause anywhere. Garman installs and converts our data at the Authorized Locations (§ 4(a)–(b)) and its personnel work with our operations (§ 9). *Proposal:* fallback-level covenant as a new § 20(j) — E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy USD 2,000,000 — leaving preferred-level CGL, workers' compensation and certificate mechanics for negotiation.

### Compliant positions to preserve

EXCLUSIVITY, NONCOMPETE, MFN, MINCOMMIT, LD and AUDIT are all clean: no sourcing restriction, field-of-use restraint, price-matching mechanic, committed spend, penalty or vendor audit right binds us. AUDIT is better than our preferred position and we should not add an audit mechanic, as doing so would only create an obligation against us. T4C sits at the fallback (90 days rather than 30, and no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees) but Garman has no convenience right at all, which exceeds preferred; we are not redlining these minor points.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points the playbook treats as walk-away or approaching walk-away, and they should be resolved before signature:

1. **Blanket bar on Sparkling assignment (§ 3(c), with § 20(d)).** A prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out approaches walk-away territory under ASSIGN.
2. **Mutual no-hire covering all employees (§ 19).** A no-hire covering all personnel is walk-away territory under NOSOLICIT.
3. **No vendor insurance (absent from § 20).** An uninsured vendor installing software and converting our data at our sites is walk-away territory under INSURANCE.

We also flag the **wholly uncapped liability position in § 15** as our highest-priority commercial issue: it is scored critical, and while the finding does not classify it as walk-away, we should not sign without an aggregate cap.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviations and three missing clauses, sequenced so that the § 15 cap, the § 3(c)/§ 20(d) assignment fix, the § 19 non-solicit rewrite and the § 20(j) insurance covenant lead the discussion as our must-haves.
2. **Confirm the internal position on the IP/licence package** (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, with use/modify/sublicense rights and coverage of Improvements and Modifications) before we table it, and re-read the IP redline against the finding, which was repaired during verification.
3. **Obtain and review Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule), which is not reproduced in the text we reviewed.** Confirm it contains no stipulated early-termination amount, minimum annual spend or committed seat/location count, which would change the LD and MINCOMMIT conclusions. Licence-fee instalments for the perpetual licence would not themselves be a minimum commitment.
4. **Confirm Schedule "D" (Modifications) scope** in light of the IP finding that Garman owns the Modifications we pay for.
5. **Hold governing law as a tradeable item.** New York law and exclusive New York County jurisdiction is our ask; there is no arbitration clause to displace, so this is a straight forum negotiation.
6. **Preserve the clean positions.** In any counter-drafting round, resist the introduction of exclusivity, MFN, minimum-commitment, audit or liquidated-damages language, and resist any Garman change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, none of which exists today."}
